plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, fragrant, bowl-shaped to double flowers atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed dark green foliage. A beloved cut flower and garden staple in temperate climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; widely cultivated across temperate North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for over 100 years, and in China they have been cultivated for more than 1,500 years as symbols of prosperity and honor.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with dense, conical clusters of intensely fragrant tubular flowers and heart-shaped leaves. Peak bloom in many northern regions occurs in mid-May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to late May depending on latitude)
plants.location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula in southeastern Europe; cultivated throughout cool temperate regions of North America, Europe, and northern Asia
plants.funFact: Lilac is in the olive family (Oleaceae), making it a relative of jasmine and ash trees, and its scent is a classic ingredient in perfumery.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small understory tree whose pea-like magenta-pink flowers burst directly from bare branches and trunks, followed by heart-shaped leaves. In cooler northern parts of its range, blooms can linger into mid-May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late spring (March to May)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from southern Ontario to northern Mexico
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a mild tangy flavor; they are sometimes added to salads, and the trees are a flowering example of cauliflory, producing blooms directly on old wood.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like leaves and spectacular clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Northern Hemisphere subtropics, such as parts of southern California, Mexico, and the Mediterranean, it begins flowering in late spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in California, Mexico, Florida, the Mediterranean, Africa, and Australia
plants.funFact: Fallen jacaranda blossoms create purple carpets beneath the trees, and in Pretoria, South Africa, the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of trees.
